name: SOMATOM Definition Flash dual-source CT
description: Siemens developed a second-generation dual-source X-ray CT scanner with two continuously rotating tube-detector systems, a higher slice count per rotation and a high-pitch spiral acquisition mode.

date.basis: Date of the FDA clearance letter.

events.statement: The U.S. FDA issued its 510(k) clearance letter for the Siemens dual-source scanner filed as SOMATOM P47 and subsequently identified as SOMATOM Definition Flash.
events.caveats: The clearance establishes U.S. authorization and existence of the documented model. Its date does not date purchase or routine patient use.

evidence.supports: Describes the dual-source system and dates the clearance.
Explicitly identifies K082220 as the earlier SOMATOM Definition Flash clearance.
Reports the higher acquisition speed and high-pitch mode.

earliest_record.rationale: The clearance has a precise date, and the later submission ties its filing name to the commercial model.

links.statement: Definition Flash retained the Definition scanner’s dual-source layout and increased the number of slices acquired per rotation.
links.scope: Second-generation geometry in the Siemens dual-source family.

evidence.supports: Names Definition as a predicate and confirms that the new scanner retains paired rotating tube-detector systems.

evidence.locator: SOMATOM Definition and Definition Flash sections
evidence.supports: Describes the design improvements across Siemens's first and second dual-source systems.
Independent clinical observations document both dual-source models and compare paired 64- and 128-slice configurations.
